text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; to begin my evaluation, how long has this symptom been present, and did it start suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Gamekeeper's Thumb / Skier's Thumb (Ulnar Collateral Ligament Injury of the MCP joint of the Right Ring Finger).

*Correction:* Given the location is the **ring finger** (not the thumb as in the classic "Gamekeeper's" name), the diagnosis is an **Ulnar Collateral Ligament (UCL) Injury of the Right Ring Finger MCP Joint**, likely a partial or complete tear given the mechanism of forceful abduction/pulling.

I will now confirm if you felt a distinct "pop" or "snap" at the moment of injury and if there is significant tenderness on the inner (ulnar) side of the knuckle.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
